newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses recover some poise, dlr stronger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses recover some poise, dlr stronger.

text.p: European stock markets regained a little nerve and clawed back some of their steep early losses on Monday but investors remained on edge as Wall Street made an unsteady opening.

On currency markets, the dollar climbed strongly as bargain-hunters recaptured some of the ground lost on Friday. Sterling also rebounded from Friday's dramatic falls but traders said the markets was still jittery ahead of UK inflation data later this week.

London, Frankfurt and Paris stocks all tumbled by about one percent at the opening before regaining some composure. They had been badly rattled by New York's two percent fall on Friday, which spraked fears that the bull run on both sides of the Atlantic was slowing.

London, helped by benign inflation data, struggled back onto positive territory by mid-afternoon after starting 64.9 points down at 4,966.4 on the FTSE 100 index. But an uncertain start on Wall Street nudged it back into the minus column.

As the market, Europe's biggest, flitted in and out of profit, investors were growing increasingly nervous about whether the surge in London blue-chip shares, up 33 percent in the last year, had finally run out of steam.
"The market's nervous about whether it's peaked and despite the drop on Friday, the FTSE (100) was up about 130 points on the week so things look rather vulnerable," said another dealer.

In Frankfurt, stocks opened with losses of about one percent but recovered some ground. Floor trade ended down about 0.50 percent and the after-hours, computerised IBIS index was showing small losses by mid-afternoon.
Paris too bounced back from its early losses and was down only 0.25 percent in the afternoon. "It's relatively calm, it's not a huge sell-off," equity salesman John Fordyce at Oddo said.

In currency markets, the dollar gathered momentum on the mark and the yen, correcting some of Friday's fall when it plunged four pfennigs and over four yen in sympathy with the decline in U.S. asset markets.

The U.S. currency climbed more than one pfennig to 1.8570 marks and half a yen to 115.92 and dealers said the dollar outlook was good, with U.S. economic fundamentals outshining those of Germany and Japan.

Dollar bulls were encouraged by the currency's bounce-back after falling four pfennings and nearly four yen on Friday mainly because of talk that the Bundesbank might increase the repurchase rate from 3.00 percent at Tuesday's repo tender.
Dealers had expected a correction after the dollar had rallied sharply in recent weeks and Friday's sell-off was seen by many as a buying oppportunity.
"We're seeing some pretty nice short-covering, people are still interested to pick up some cheap dollars," said Ben Strauss, vice president at Bank Julius Baer.

The summer holiday period has reduced the number of players in the market and increased volatility. "Nervousness will continue even though at this stage people are more inclined to be buyers than sellers," said Chris Furness, foreign exchange strategist at 4Cast Ltd in London.

The British pound rebounded three pfennigs to 2.9455 marks and was up two cents to $1.5884 from Friday's dramatic falls. Sterling has been badly hit by official signals that British interest rates had peaked for the time being.
"There was something of an over-reaction last week in a thin market," Stewart Newnham, International Economist at First Chicago, said.

Sterling reached an eight-year peak of 3.0878 marks last month, when most analysts felt it was overvalued. Traders said the market was sitting on its hands ahead of a sensitive U.K. data late this week

But some remained upbeat. Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist for Europe at Bank of America, said: The pound is pretty much at a bottom now. Over the next few months we could be looking at a move up towards three marks again."
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8570 marks and 115.92 yen, compared with 1.8453 and 115.12 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 0.1 points at 5,031.2.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed 21.02 points down at 4,333.13 in bourse floor trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 21.03 points at 2,974.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $327.20 an ounce, up from Friday's London close of $325.05. Silver was at $4.44, up three cents.
